summary: Despite its title, this clipped cppreference.com page is the reference index for the C++ Concurrency support library (since C++11), not the Ranges library. It lists the library's components grouped into threads, atomic operations, mutual exclusion, condition variables, semaphores, latches and barriers, futures, and safe reclamation, with the C++ standard version each one was introduced in. The page is mostly navigation and tables, and it gives only a brief overview of the library's purpose.
one_line: Reference index of the C++ Concurrency support library, covering threads, atomics, mutexes, condition variables, semaphores, futures and safe reclamation.
key_facts: The Concurrency support library is marked as (since C++11) on the cppreference.com page.
The page states that C++ includes built-in support for threads, atomic operations, mutual exclusion, condition variables, and futures.
The std::thread class (C++11) manages a separate thread, and threads enable programs to execute across several processor cores.
The std::jthread class (C++20) is std::thread with support for auto-joining and cancellation.
The stop_token, stop_source and stop_callback types (all C++20) are designed to enable thread cancellation for std::jthread.
The stop_token, stop_source and stop_callback types can also be used independently of std::jthread, for example to interrupt std::condition_variable_any waiting functions.

The hardware_destructive_interference_size constant (C++17) gives the minimum offset to avoid false sharing, and hardware_constructive_interference_size gives the maximum offset to promote true sharing.
The this_thread namespace functions yield, get_id, sleep_for and sleep_until are all marked C++11.
The atomic class template (C++11) provides specializations for bool, integral, floating-point (since C++20) and pointer types, and atomic_ref (C++20) provides atomic operations on non-atomic objects.
The atomic_wait and atomic_notify_one/atomic_notify_all function templates are C++20 additions for blocking a thread until an atomic value changes.
Mutual exclusion types include mutex and timed_mutex (C++11), shared_mutex (C++17) and shared_timed_mutex (C++14), all defined in the mutex and shared_mutex headers.
The generic mutex management types include lock_guard (C++11), scoped_lock (C++17), unique_lock (C++11) and shared_lock (C++14).
The counting_semaphore and binary_semaphore types are C++20, and the latch and barrier types are also C++20.
The Safe Reclamation section lists read-copy-update (RCU) and hazard pointer components marked C++26, and their pages are shown as not existing on the site.
